## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sukajātaka* (Ja 255) is a narrative included in the Jātaka collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka [Catalog]. According to the traditional introductory narrative, the Buddha recounted this story while residing at Jetavana with reference to a monk who died from overeating. Within environmental and ethical discussions of the Jātaka stories, the text serves as a cautionary tale against greed and excessive consumption: it relates the story of a parrot that developed an excessive craving for mangoes on a distant island, ignored his father's warnings, became exhausted on his return flight, fell into the water, and was eaten by a fish [UNDV Conference Volume 2009].

 However, DharmaNexus identifies low-scoring machine text alignments with Haribhaṭṭa's *Jātakamālā* (*Haribhaṭṭajātakamālā*, D4152) in the Tibetan Tengyur [DharmaNexus].
